intro: Picture waking up, opening your door, and finding a calm, clear lagoon with fish swimming through a tropical garden and limestone cliffs rising up behind it — all of it just a few minutes' walk from Ao Nang Beach · Peace Laguna Resort & Spa is a 4-star garden resort that sits right in the middle of Ao Nang, with rooms and cottages arranged around a garden lagoon, so it feels shadier and quieter than the usual roadside high-rise hotels · What guests talk about most is the calm garden atmosphere in the middle of a busy tourist town, paired with a location that's about 200 m walk to the beach and the Ao Nang walking street · There are 3 pools, a spa, and rooms across several tiers from standard rooms up to waterside cottages, from around ฿2,200/night, scored 8.4 from 89 reviews on Trip.com

body.html: Who Peace Laguna suits — the shortest possible summary is that Peace Laguna Resort & Spa is a resort for people who want "the calm of a garden resort" but don't want to cut themselves off from the convenience of Ao Nang · It's not a roadside high-rise selling sea views from the balcony, and it's not a five-star luxury resort that whisks you off to a private beach · It's a 4-star resort designed so the rooms and cottages are spread out around a clear lagoon in a tropical garden, with Ao Nang's limestone cliffs as a natural backdrop · From real reviews across several platforms, the people who say they love it most are families with young kids, couples after a relaxed vibe, and working-age travellers who want somewhere shady to stay but can easily walk out to eat and explore · A lot of first-time Krabi visitors pick this place because it sits right in the middle — no risk of staying far from town, but no putting up with road noise all night either · On the flip side, anyone hunting for a brand-new, modern-in-every-corner hotel, or wanting an infinity pool with a sea view like the ones on social media, may feel this place is a touch "classic," because it leans on trees, the lagoon, and a natural feel more than flash · To put it plainly, Peace Laguna delivers fully on "calm and shady in a convenient location," and that's why it's stayed on travellers' radar for years

Location and getting around — this is one of Peace Laguna's top strengths, and the reviews agree on it · The resort sits at 193 Moo 2 in Ao Nang, Mueang Krabi, set back just a little from the main road so it stays quiet, but still about 200 m or roughly a 5 min walk to Ao Nang Beach, with the walking street, restaurants, massage shops, and tour counters all an easy stroll away · Many international reviews praise this kind of location as "the best of both worlds" — you come back to the resort and it's quiet, like you've slipped out of town, but when you want food or a boat trip it's just a few minutes' walk · Getting further afield is easy too: Ao Nang pier for island trips and Railay is a short walk, Nopparat Thara Beach is about a 10 min drive, Krabi town is about a 25–30 min drive, and it's about a 30 min drive from Krabi Airport (KBV) · One small note from reviews is that the resort sits down a lane you have to walk in from the main road a little, so anyone dragging heavy bags or travelling with elderly guests may want to use the transfer service or ask the resort for help on arrival

"I woke up, pulled back the curtains, and there was the lagoon and green trees with fish swimming in the water — so quiet I forgot the busy Ao Nang Beach was a five-minute walk away. It really does balance calm with convenience."

Room types and decor — Peace Laguna has around 149 rooms and cottages across several tiers to suit your budget and needs · It starts with the Standard Room at around 36 sqm, the entry-level option in the main building, good for couples or travellers focused on value · Stepping up is the Superior Room at around 50–55 sqm, which is roomier and gets more of the garden feel · And the highlight many reviews recommend is the Superior Cottage and Deluxe Cottage at around 70 sqm, standalone cottages spread out beside the lagoon and through the garden, giving a private feel like having your own little house · What reviews consistently praise is that the rooms and cottages are bigger than you'd expect at this price, with a private balcony or terrace, and many have seating that looks out over the garden or lagoon · Every room has air conditioning, a flat-screen TV with satellite channels, a fridge/minibar, a separate seating corner, and free Wi-Fi · The decor is classic tropical-resort with wood tones and warm colours, leaning toward blending in with the garden rather than modern minimalism · To be honest, some reviews note that the resort has been open for a fair while, and parts of the rooms and around the pools are starting to show their age and need some upkeep, so if you want the best-condition room, ask for a recently renovated one or step up to a cottage tier

Facilities, pools, and spa — the highlight that sets Peace Laguna apart from other places in the area is having three outdoor pools spread through the garden, one of which looks out at the limestone cliffs behind, which many reviews call the resort's best spot for photos and lounging · Having several pools means it rarely feels crowded even when the resort is full, and there's a pool that's good for kids so families can relax · Beyond the pools there's Maya Spa offering massages and treatments, a fitness room, sauna, table-tennis room, pool bar, and café · For anyone who loves a natural setting, the garden and lagoon in the middle of the resort are a relaxation space in their own right — easy for a morning stroll or sipping coffee by the water · There's an airport transfer (ask about the cost in advance), a tour counter to help arrange island trips, and parking · A common note in reviews is that the Wi-Fi signal isn't very strong in some spots, especially the cottages set deep in the garden, and because it's a resort with lots of trees and water, there can be mosquitoes at times — both of which you can handle by bringing mosquito spray and asking for a room near the common areas if you really need heavy internet

Food and bars — the resort has two main restaurants serving Thai and international food, plus a pool bar and café · The thing that earns the most praise in reviews is the breakfast buffet, which many say is varied and filling, with Thai, Asian, and Western options as well as live-cooking stations · The open-air dining room catching the garden breeze makes breakfast feel relaxed · For other meals, the resort's location helps a lot, because a few minutes' walk gets you to all the seafood spots, Thai restaurants, international restaurants, and bars of Ao Nang, so many people eat breakfast at the resort and head out for lunch and dinner · The garden pool bar is good for a cold drink after a swim or a full day out · Overall, food at Peace Laguna isn't the reason you come to eat in the resort, but it's a nicely done extra, especially breakfast, and it fits a style of stay where you use the resort as a base to explore Ao Nang

Service — service is another point that earns steady praise in real reviews · Many staff get a mention for being friendly, smiley, and helpful, with island trips, calling cars, restaurant recommendations, and sorting out on-the-spot problems · On Booking.com the staff score is as high as around 8.9, which shows service is a strength guests genuinely feel · Many families say the team is attentive to young kids and good at helping with extra beds or children's items · For fairness, a few voices in reviews say that when the resort is full or several groups check in at once, the wait can get longer, and attention to detail isn't equally consistent across every department · But overall, service is still an advantage here, and one of the reasons many guests say they'd come back

What real reviews say (praise and gripes) — pulling from Trip.com, Booking.com, and TripAdvisor, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: the calm, shady garden and lagoon atmosphere, the central Ao Nang location within walking distance of the beach and restaurants, three pools that rarely feel crowded plus one with a limestone-cliff view, rooms and cottages bigger than the price with private balconies, a varied breakfast, and staff who are friendly and helpful (the location score on Booking is around 9.2 and staff around 8.9) · On the notes side: the most frequently mentioned is a Wi-Fi signal that isn't strong in some spots, especially the cottages deep in the garden · Next is mosquitoes and insects in some seasons, which is normal for a resort with lots of trees and water · And some reviews note the resort has been open a fair while, with parts of the rooms and around the pools starting to look old and needing upkeep, plus linen cleanliness that should sometimes be improved · Most of these gripes are things you can manage by choosing the right room tier, preparing for mosquitoes, and setting expectations to match a classic garden resort, rather than big problems that keep people from coming back

"The pools are gorgeous, especially the one with the limestone-cliff view, and the staff were lovely and arranged a boat trip for us. The only downside is the internet in the room was a bit slow when we were in the back cottage, but if you're really here to relax it doesn't bother you at all."

Price comparison and value — the starting rate for a Standard Room is around ฿2,200/night at normal pricing (on some platforms you'll see promotional starting rates of around 49–72 dollars per night), and it can climb to around ฿3,500–5,000+ in high season or over long weekends · Superior rooms and lagoon-side cottages sit from around ฿3,000 up into several thousand depending on size and timing · Compared with similarly located resorts in Ao Nang, Peace Laguna feels like good value among 4-star garden resorts that emphasise atmosphere and space, especially once you count having three pools, roomy rooms, a garden-lagoon setting that's hard to find in a central location, and a walk to the beach that saves both time and travel costs · Many reviews suggest the entry to mid-level rooms offer better value than upgrading to the very top, because the real selling point here is the common areas and location more than in-room luxury · If you plan to use Ao Nang as a base for island trips and to walk out to eat and explore every day, the money you spend on this place's location and calm is well worth it

What to know before booking — a few things will make your stay smoother · One, if you need the internet for work or online meetings, ask for a room near the common building/lobby, because the cottages deep in the garden may have a weaker Wi-Fi signal · Two, bring mosquito spray or lotion, because it's a resort with lots of trees and water, and some seasons have natural mosquitoes and insects · Three, if you want the best-condition room, ask for a recently renovated one or step up to a cottage tier, and ask about the view you want (garden view / lagoon view) when you book · Four, during Krabi's high season (November–April) Ao Nang fills up fast and prices climb quickly, so book ahead and compare across several platforms · Five, check-in is around 3:00 PM and check-out around 11:00 AM, so if you arrive in the morning or fly out late, ask about luggage storage or late check-out in advance · Six, choose free cancellation if your plans aren't firm, because prices tend to change with the season

Verdict — from all the real reviews, Peace Laguna Resort & Spa is best suited to people who want a calm, shady tropical garden atmosphere beside a lagoon, in a location that's still a few minutes' walk to the beach and the buzz of Ao Nang · Three pools, a lagoon setting with limestone-cliff views, roomy rooms and cottages, friendly service, and a varied breakfast make it a good-value choice among the area's 4-star garden resorts · If you're after a brand-new, modern-in-every-corner hotel, an infinity pool with a sea view, or strong internet in every nook, this might not be your answer, and you should consider a clifftop stay or a luxury beachfront resort instead · But for a Krabi trip where you want the calm of a garden resort plus a central Ao Nang location at an affordable price — Peace Laguna answers that need well, and it's why it still scores well and keeps drawing repeat guests after years

honestSummary: Peace Laguna Resort & Spa is a resort that sells a calm tropical garden atmosphere beside a lagoon with limestone-cliff views, in a central Ao Nang location within walking distance of the beach and restaurants · You get both shady privacy and the convenience of a tourist area, plus three pools and friendly service at an affordable price · But you have to accept it's a classic garden resort that's been open a while, with weak Wi-Fi in spots, natural mosquitoes, and parts starting to look old — this is a place that's worth it if you pick a good room and set expectations to match a garden-resort style
honestChecks: If you need the internet for work / online meetings — Wi-Fi isn't strong in some spots, especially cottages deep in the garden → ask for a room near the common building/lobby and bring a backup mobile data SIM

If you're sensitive to mosquitoes and insects — it's a garden resort with lots of trees and water, and some seasons have natural mosquitoes → bring your own mosquito spray/lotion and close doors and windows in the evening

If you want a brand-new, modern-in-every-corner room — the resort has been open a while and parts are starting to look old → ask for a recently renovated room or step up to a cottage tier, and set your expectations mainly on the garden atmosphere and location

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Peace Laguna Resort & Spa Krabi

faq.q: Where is Peace Laguna Resort & Spa, and can you walk to the beach?
faq.a: It's at 193 Moo 2 in the heart of Ao Nang, Mueang Krabi, set back just a little from the main road so it stays quiet · It's about 200 m or roughly a 5 min walk to Ao Nang Beach · You can walk to the walking street, restaurants, and Ao Nang pier · Nopparat Thara Beach is about a 10 min drive, and Krabi Airport (KBV) is about a 30 min drive

faq.q: What's the starting price at Peace Laguna Resort & Spa, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around ฿2,200/night for a Standard Room of around 36 sqm at normal pricing · There's a Superior Room of around 50–55 sqm and Superior/Deluxe Cottages of around 70 sqm, which are standalone cottages by the lagoon · High-season (Nov–Apr) prices climb fast, so compare across several platforms before booking

faq.q: How many pools does the resort have, and what's there to use?
faq.a: There are three outdoor pools spread through the garden, one of which looks out at the limestone cliffs behind · Beyond the pools there's Maya Spa, a fitness room, sauna, table-tennis room, pool bar, and café · The highlight is the garden and clear lagoon in the middle of the resort, where you can stroll and relax

It's a great fit for families with young kids, couples, and anyone who wants a calm, shady garden-resort atmosphere but can still walk to the beach and restaurants · It suits people coming to relax and use Ao Nang as a base for island trips · If you're after a brand-new modern hotel, an infinity pool with a sea view, or strong internet everywhere, a clifftop stay or a luxury beachfront resort may suit you better

faq.q: What are the Wi-Fi and mosquitoes like at Peace Laguna?
faq.a: Many reviews note that the Wi-Fi signal isn't strong in some spots, especially the cottages deep in the garden — if you need heavy internet, ask for a room near the common areas and bring a backup mobile SIM · Because it's a garden resort with lots of trees and water, some seasons may have natural mosquitoes and insects, so bring your own mosquito spray or lotion

faq.q: What are Peace Laguna Resort & Spa's review scores like?
faq.a: It scored 8.4 from 89 reviews on Trip.com · Booking.com is around 8.1 (location around 9.2 and staff around 8.9) · TripAdvisor ranks it #16 of 202 hotels in Ao Nang/Krabi · Overall it's a resort praised for its location, garden atmosphere, and service, while the main notes are Wi-Fi in some spots and the building's age
